subject: Dedicated capacity — performance guardrails & pilot commitment plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Abby Moreno <abby@pioneerhealth.com>; Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — performance guardrails & pilot commitment plan

Hi Abby / Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and concrete next steps so we all have alignment on the SLO targets & validation approach for a Dedicated capacity pilot. I kept this intentionally short and action-oriented.

Key SLO targets you called out during the demo:
- 95th pct latency: 150 ms (token-level streaming, typical prompt length ~120 tokens)
- P99 latency: goal <= 400 ms for single-turn, non-streaming workloads
- Concurrent qps baseline: 80 sustained across the cluster during peak windows; spiky bursts to 160 qps acceptable with burst capacity
- Token throughput: estimated 2.4M tokens/day for the initial vertical (user search + real-time summarization)

What Redwood will validate in the pilot (proposal):
1) Reserved throughput sizing: run pre-prod workload simulation for 72 hours to validate sustained 80 qps at 95th pct latency <= 150 ms.
2) GPU comparison matrix: benchmark 2x A800-80GB (fp16 quantized baseline) vs 4x A100-40GB (higher concurrency) for streaming and KV cache behavior.
3) Streaming tail analysis: measure streaming chunking latency and first-byte latency for typical prompts and larger context (~1k tokens).
4) Failure / fallback behavior: verify automated fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constraints hit 95pct utilization.

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 12: share pilot metrics template + GPU matrix (I attached an initial matrix for Ben to fill with bench numbers)
- Nov 16–18: Redwood runs quick bench pass in our lab and returns numbers + recommended pool size
- Nov 23: kickoff pilot in your QA environment (3 weeks) with joint monitoring and daily stand for first 4 business days

Immediate asks from PioneerHealth:
- Confirm that the 95th/99th targets above reflect your internal SLAs (reply inline if any change).
- Provide a sample of representative prompt mixes (percent of short/medium/long requests) and typical payload sizes.

Attachments: gpu_matrix_v1.xlsx (benchmark template), pilot-metrics-template.csv

Thanks — I’ll hand off the bench to Ben once we get your prompt mix and confirm SLOs.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

From: Abby Moreno <abby@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — performance guardrails & pilot commitment plan

Thanks Karthik — this is perfect and captures our expectations. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Confirm 95th = 150 ms is for streaming-first experiences (first byte + steady chunking). For non-streaming API calls, P95 can be relaxed to 220 ms as long as P99 stays <= 400 ms.
- Our peak concurrency is actually bursty around 120 qps for the mental-health triage service — we should set the trial burst target to 200 qps to be safe.
- Token mix: 60% short (<=60 tokens), 30% medium (60–250 tokens), 10% long (250–1,000 tokens).

We can deliver a sanitized sample of prompts by Nov 13 EOD. Samir — can you confirm procurement lead time for any contractual guardrails (SOW / pilot terms)?

Appreciate the clarity. Looking forward to the bench numbers.

— Abby
Abby Moreno
Director, Product Integrations | PioneerHealth
abby@pioneerhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — performance guardrails & pilot commitment plan

Karthik / team — I ran an initial pass in the lab overnight and attached high-level numbers in gpu_matrix_v1.xlsx. Summary points below (full matrix attached):

- A800-80GB (quantized, continuous batching): best steady-state cost per token and good for sustained 80–120 qps with 95th around 140–170 ms depending on prompt length; streaming first-byte excellent (60–85 ms).
- A100-40GB (higher concurrency with sharding): better at handling spikes >120 qps without increasing p95 much; P99 tail improves for very short prompts but suffers slightly for long-context streaming due to KV memory overhead.
- Recommendation: Pilot runs with a hybrid pool: 2 x A800 + 2 x A100. A800 covers steady throughput/cost, A100 provides headroom for spikes and improves fallbacks.

Operational notes:
- With the proposed hybrid pool, reserved throughput of 160 qps headroom maps to ~2.4M tokens/day (matches their estimate).
- I included a sample pilot run config in pilot-metrics-template.csv that maps traffic mix -> batch configs -> expected SLO headroom.

Next steps from infra bench side: I’ll schedule a longer 72-hour run (Nov 16–19) in our staging cluster using PioneerHealth sample prompts once we get them. Expect final numbers and an ops-runbook for cutover by Nov 20.

Attachments: gpu_matrix_v1.xlsx, pilot-metrics-template.csv

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Abby Moreno <abby@pioneerhealth.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — performance guardrails & pilot commitment plan

Thanks, everyone — aligned. Quick summary of actions and ownership so nothing slips: 

1) PioneerHealth: share sanitized prompt sample + confirmation on burst target (Abby) — due Nov 13 EOD.
2) PioneerHealth: procurement point (Samir) to confirm PO window & any pilot SOW clauses around performance credits — pls reply by Nov 16.
3) Redwood bench: Ben to run 72-hour run (Nov 16–19) with the sample prompts and circulate finalized gpu_matrix and recommended pool sizing by Nov 20.
4) Redwood ops: Monica to draft a short cutover/runbook and canary checklist for pilot launch (Nov 23) — deliverable by Nov 20.
5) Engineering / Rollout: Lauren to prepare monitoring dashboard with token-level cost, 95/99 percentiles, and streaming first-byte metric for daily stand tracking — initial dashboard by Nov 22.

If Abby confirms the slight relaxation for non-streaming P95 (220 ms) we’ll encode that into the pilot gating checks. Also proposing a short daily 15-min standup for the first 4 business days after Nov 23 (Mon–Thu) — I’ll calendar that once procurement timing is clear.

Thanks again — this is a good path to get PioneerHealth into a predictable Dedicated flow without overprovisioning.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
